summary.text: 诉 is the simplified form of 訴. In 訴, 言 marks speech or reporting, while historical analyses disagree about the identity and sound role of the right side.

formation.text: Traditional 訴 is analyzed as phonosemantic: 言 contributes the speech or reporting category, and the right side is proposed as a sound element. The received Shuowen analysis names 厈省; Song editors reject that analysis, while Duan Yucai proposes a graphic path from 㡿 through 厈 to 斥. The path and historical sound fit remain uncertain.

components.text: In 诉, visible 讠 is the simplified counterpart of 訁 and contributes the speech or reporting category. Traditional 訴 uses 言 in that role; the evidence does not establish a direct positional-form relationship between 言 and 讠.

Traditional 訴 has visible 斥 on the right. The received Shuowen analysis identifies 厈省 as phonetic; Duan Yucai instead proposes that 㡿 changed to 厈 in clerical writing and was later miswritten as 斥. This proposed history is not confirmed by an early specimen.

sound_limitation.text: The cited historical reconstructions for 㡿 and 訴 differ and do not establish the proposed ancient sound fit. Their modern Mandarin readings also do not establish it.

sound.text: The checked Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give distinct Middle Chinese readings; this comparison does not demonstrate the proposed phonetic fit.
The checked Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give distinct Old Chinese readings; this comparison does not demonstrate the proposed phonetic fit.
Modern Mandarin readings are chì for 斥 and sù for 訴; these current readings do not settle their historical sound relationship.

history.text: For traditional 訴, the received Shuowen analysis names 厈省 as the sound element. Song editors dispute this, while Duan Yucai proposes the direction 㡿 → 厈 → 斥. This is a commentator’s proposed graphic history, not a sequence confirmed by an early specimen.
In simplified 诉, the left-side 讠 corresponds by simplification to 訁. This graphic change is separate from the disputed right-side history of traditional 訴.

uncertainties.text: Historical analyses differ over the right side’s identity and sound role. The proposed 㡿-to-訴 phonetic fit remains unresolved.

The Shuowen cites an Analects phrase, but its exact graph in a securely dated manuscript witness is not established. No securely dated oracle-bone, bronze, or Warring States specimen of 訴 is identified here.
The simplified-form classification is explicit, though the inspected portion of the general 1956 scheme does not show a character-specific standardization entry for 訴/诉.

senses.text: The Shuowen glosses 訴 as 告, “report” or “tell,” and cites an Analects passage. The citation is a traditional textual reference, not a securely dated manuscript witness.

senses.gloss: report a grievance; bring a complaint
senses.text: A passage cited from the Hanshu Chengdi annals uses 訴 for reporting grievances at court, supporting an early imperial attestation of this use.
Historical citations include uses glossed as accusation or denunciation; their chronology relative to grievance reporting is unresolved.
Cited examples are glossed as expressing or telling feelings. Their chronological relationship to reporting or accusation is unresolved.
A recorded use means seeking recourse, but its date and relationship to the other uses are unresolved.
Current dictionary glosses include accusation, suing, informing, and narrating; this range does not establish a chronological sequence of meanings.

limitations.text: Cited examples attest grievance reporting, accusation or denunciation, expressing or telling feelings, and seeking recourse, but do not establish a chronological path among these uses.
The early imperial label refers to the Hanshu passage cited by a dictionary. The Shuowen also cites an Analects phrase, but its surviving witness is not dated here.

overview.text: 诉 is the simplified form of 訴, used for reporting or telling, including bringing a grievance. Its left side, 讠, marks the speech category; the traditional form’s right side has competing sound analyses, and its proposed history remains uncertain.

components.text: 讠 is the simplified counterpart of 訁 and marks the speech or reporting category.
Duan Yucai proposed that 訴’s right side changed from 㡿 through 厈 to 斥; other analyses differ, and this path is unconfirmed.

relationships.text: In simplified 诉, 讠 contributes the speech or reporting category and corresponds by simplification to 訁 in traditional 訴.
诉 is explicitly classified as the simplified counterpart of 訴.

In traditional 訴, one analysis treats the right side as a sound element: the received Shuowen account identifies 厈省, while Duan Yucai proposes that 㡿 changed through 厈 to visible 斥. The identity and historical sound fit remain disputed.
